findings.claim: The doc comment of sourceAnswers was not updated for the new LineageError branch: a failing Candidates listing now counts as answering when the failure is a LineageError. The Source fallback path, `Memories(project)` for a source without a Prober, has no such exemption, so a non-Prober source whose Memories fails with a LineageError would still be reported as MemoryUnavailable. No such source exists today. The two branches are inconsistent and the rule is not documented where it is applied.
evidence: project_sync.go:81-93: the Candidates error is exempted only for *memory.LineageError, while `_, err := src.Memories(project); return err == nil` is not.
internal/engram/source.go:51-57,137-144: Memories also goes through build and the lineage function, so it can return the same wrapped LineageError for a source with no Prober.
internal/engram/source.go:61-64: the only real source (Engram) has a Prober, so the Memories fallback is not reached on the production path.
Read the 5cb107ef diff in full and project_sync.go, cmd/longterm-mem/lineage.go, cmd_sync.go, cmd_promote.go, app.go, internal/engram/source.go.
Traced LineageError through engram.build -> Source.Candidates -> promote.Sync (%w), so errors.As in sourceAnswers matches.
Dry run, explicit promote and MCP promote never reach MemoryUnavailable for a lineage error.
Hook (engine/synctrigger/synctrigger.go:324-341): a lineage failure moves from failure:engram-unavailable (exit 4) to exit 1, the intended change.
memory.LineageError is constructed only at lineage.go:35 and 39 (memorycard reads), so no non-lineage failure is misclassified.
